pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome – St Mary and St John CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St Mary and St John CE Primary School!
It is a real privilege to be the Headteacher of such a vibrant and caring school. We are an inclusive, richly diverse two-form entry city school, in the heart of East Oxford. At Mary and John, our vision is to help children to do everything in love, striving to be the best that they can be in an environment where they feel safe, healthy, engaged, supported and challenged as they learn and achieve. Our aim is for every child to be inspired and motivated, so that they thrive in their learning and want to achieve more. Our friendly and hard-working team are committed to every child achieving in all areas of school life.
Set next to The Kidneys, there is an abundance of greenery all around, and yet we are only a short walk from Oxford City with its many cultural resources which enrich our curriculum. We are fortunate to have a spacious site which has undergone recent refurbishments. We are delighted with the improvements to our learning environment, including a beautiful library at the heart of the school.
Our Reception children joined us at Meadow Lane for the first time in September 2023. We are excited to now be together as a Reception through to Year 6 school on the same site! However, we continue to have great links with Comper School and children.
Walt Disney famously said, “I dream, I test my dreams against my beliefs, I dare to take risks, and I execute my vision to make those dreams come true.” I believe this encapsulates our school: dreaming big, testing those dreams against a shared set of beliefs before taking calculated risks to see our vision fulfilled. We have a passion for education and believe learning should be contagious. This passion spills out to the children and adults with whom we work, sparking a curiosity and drive to reach their full potential. We believe in holistic learning experiences, growing children who are inquisitive about the world around them, the difference they can make, and ensuring they are excited to learn more each day.
At Mary and John, you will find:
All underpinned by the core values of love, respect, empathy, courage and aspiration.
Our Ofsted inspection in May 2023, judged Mary & John as a Good School which is a fantastic achievement within the new framework. The report speaks to our ethos and vision as a school, and I hope you will experience this when you visit.
Pupils enjoy attending and learning at this inclusive school. Pupils have good attitudes to their learning. The school values of ‘love, respect, empathy, courage, aspiration, and curiosity’ permeate the curriculum and wider activity in the school.
Leaders plan for all pupils to leave the school as ‘curious lifelong learners’ who have built up resilience so that they are better equipped to deal with any challenges they may face.
We hope this website gives you a feel of our school, but do come and see for yourselves. Please do not hesitate to contact the school office on 01865 723841 to make an appointment. We look forward to seeing you very soon!
Please enjoy the video tour below of our lovely school.
If, after watching it, you have any questions for us, please do not hesitate to contact us.

Curriculum Design and Coverage
We are committed to making St Mary & St John an inclusive environment, fostering curiosity, spirituality, creativity and respect. At our school we want everyone to be valued, to explore the joy of learning, and to achieve their full potential. Children at St Mary and St John celebrate the richness of diversity within our school community. They are confident, empathetic, and resilient, able to take measured risks with a sense of self-belief. We strive to empower the children at school, motivating them in an environment where they feel valued and understand the power of being inquisitive. When they leave us, they will be enthusiastic life-long learners who are ambitious, courageous and able to build positive, healthy relationships.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra-Curricular Activities – St Mary and St John CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music at St Mary & St John
Music is an important part of the school curriculum, and all children take part in singing and general music sessions in school. Some children may also wish to join the Mary & John Orchestra Strings Group or sing with the choir.
For children who would like to learn a musical instrument in school, Oxfordshire Music Service and some school specific music teachers provide a range of lessons.
Oxfordshire Music Service website
Sports & Outdoor Learning at St Mary & St John
We have a sports coach who leads sports activities for Key Stage 2 children at lunchtime each day. The children are given the opportunity to take part in sports festivals and sports competitions. We have a boys and girls football team who train weekly and play regularly.
Every year our Year 6 children go on a fun filled residential trip to Woodlands Centre in Wales. When the children stay at the centre they have a week of outdoor activities including: canoeing, climbing, abseiling, mountain walking, orienteering and caving. This week is often one of the highlights of the children’s year.

Remote Learning at St Mary and St John Primary School – St Mary and St John CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Remote Education Provision (Homework) Letter – September 2021
As a school, we have adapted our curriculum so that any child who needs to learn from home due to a COVID related absence, can access the same learning that is happening for the whole class.
Our remote learning plan for individual pupils isolating at home
The relevant class teacher will make work available to the pupil as soon as is practicable – we will aim for this to be before 11am. This will usually be made available using Purple Mash or the home learning section on our website.
Our first piece of advice to parents is that all children find elements of learning challenging at times so try not to worry if your child becomes stuck and you cannot explain it to them. If this happens then make a note of what they found hard and move onto another learning activity.
Home Learning Grids
In creating the Home Learning Grids, we fully acknowledge that they cannot replace the quality of learning your child receives at school, however, our focus has been on creating tasks that all children can access to maximise their learning whilst at home. Please be mindful during busy times online services may be slower.
These grids provide alternative work to Purple Mash, linked to the topic being explored in class. Some activities are more project led, giving a break from screen time. They will be updated each term with activities that children may miss if they are isolating. This work has an open-ended approach, providing children with opportunities to explore areas of personal interest within the topic. The grids are not an exhaustive list to be completed, but a ‘pick and mix’ approach that children can dip in and out of, alongside work being set on Purple Mash. There is also a suggested timetable for how to structure time, along with ideas for how to support at home.
Please do not feel this work needs to be completed if your child is feeling unwell, children are only expected to access home learning if they would be well enough to be in school but have tested positive. We hope that this supports you through the difficulty of isolation.
Home Learning Grids – Term 3 2022
Year 1 Home Learning Grid Term 4 2022
Year 2 Home Learning Grid Term 4 2022
Year 3 Home Learning Grid Term 4 2022
Year 4 Home Learning Grid Term 4 2022
Year 5 Home Learning Grid Term 4 2022
Year 6 Home Learning Grid Term 4 2022
What are the aims of the Learning Grids?
• To create age specific learning opportunities. • To create a resource for parents that is easy to access and use – the focus is on parents being able to help deliver the content or children accessing it independently. • Key learning is linked to the National Curriculum. • To enable children to continue with their learning at home during periods of isolation. • To provide structure and focus to each day.
How do I use the Learning Grids?
As a parent your first step is to select the age range linked to the year group your child is in. You then download the learning grid and begin following suggested directed activities. The aim is for you to complete a minimum of two hours of learning a day with your child but this is very much your parental choice and you may wish for your child to do more.

An additional resource we have bought into as a school is a child-friendly search engine called Espresso. Espresso is packed full of content appropriate to the children’s topics covered in school. Teachers use it in school to support the delivery of lessons, and we believe it will be a helpful resource for home learning too. It can be accessed at home using the username and password which has been emailed to parents and carers. Please contact the office if you have lost the details.

School Governors
What do school governors do?
They are responsible for:
Supporting the school’s culture and values
Promoting high standards of educational achievement
Overseeing its financial performance
Who are they?
At St Mary & St John the Governing Body has 14 members:
Three Parent Governors (elected by parents/carers)
Making Contact
We welcome comments. You can contact us in person around the school, or by e-mail (ssmjgovernors@gmail.com), or by leaving a message at the school office.
If you are interested in finding out more about becoming a governor, please contact the Clerk to the Governors. You can do this by e-mail (ssmjgovernors@gmail.com), or again by leaving a message at the school office.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum Design and Coverage
We are committed to making St Mary & St John an inclusive environment, fostering curiosity, spirituality, creativity and respect. At our school we want everyone to be valued, to explore the joy of learning, and to achieve their full potential. Children at St Mary and St John celebrate the richness of diversity within our school community. They are confident, empathetic, and resilient, able to take measured risks with a sense of self-belief. We strive to empower the children at school, motivating them in an environment where they feel valued and understand the power of being inquisitive. When they leave us, they will be enthusiastic life-long learners who are ambitious, courageous and able to build positive, healthy relationships.
Intent of St Mary and St John’s Curriculum
Implementation of St Mary and St John’s Curriculum
Lessons balance skills and knowledge.

National Curriculum
We follow the National Curriculum throughout the school. Developing children’s English and Maths is central to our teaching and learning. We spend time each day on these essential skills.
We use a cross-curricular approach to learning, when appropriate, helping children to learn in meaningful contexts, independently and in collaboration.
Wherever possible we encourage creativity and support the children in expressing themselves, in all areas of the curriculum, to develop their confidence and foster cooperation.
We place a strong emphasis on the creative arts, personal, social, health and economic education (PSHE), including e-safety, physical education and outdoor learning.
If you require additional information about the curriculum please contact the school office.
National Curriculum
Assessment
We use a system of continuous assessment as part of our daily teaching practice. Teachers assess learning throughout every lesson to identify misconceptions, adapt teaching, and ensure that all children are supported and challenged appropriately. Alongside this ongoing formative assessment, we also use summative assessments to build a fuller picture of each child’s progress over time.
All children in Years 1–6 complete NFER assessments in reading and mathematics, and children in Years 3–6 also complete NFER assessments in grammar, punctuation and spelling. Year 1 additionally complete a phonics screen based on the national phonics screening assessment. The raw scores from these tests are converted into standardised scores, which form part of the basis of our Pupil Progress Meetings, alongside a detailed report from the class teacher.
Outcomes are grouped into four attainment bands for each subject: Below Expected, Working Towards Expected, Expected, and Greater Depth.
Please note, copies of the documents on this website can be made available on request.

Exciting News! Announcing Our New Holiday Camp Partnership!
A Joint Message from St Mary & St John School, and uKids
We are absolutely thrilled to share some fantastic news with you! We are delighted to announce a brand-new partnership that will bring high-quality, fun-filled childcare directly to our school community during the holiday periods.
From February 2026, St Mary & St John School will be working hand-in-hand with uKids to provide an exceptional Holiday camp right here!
This exciting collaboration is designed to offer:
To introduce you to the heart of uKids, Nikki, their Operations Director, will be visiting our schools at the end of the school day one day this term. This will be a wonderful opportunity for you to meet her, learn more about the exciting plans for the camp, and ask any questions you may have. Keep an eye on our school notices for the exact date and time!
Discover More Online:
To get a sneak peek at the fantastic activities and services uKids will be offering, please visit their dedicated website page:
https://www.u-kids.co.uk/holiday-camps
We truly hope that this valuable new service will provide significant support to many children and families in our community.
The Teams at St Mary & St John and uKids
